A pharmacist is turning to cannabis compounds as a potential weapon against antibiotic-resistant superbugs after big pharma largely abandoned the fight against antimicrobial resistance. Purdue Pharma was sentenced and ordered to pay $5.5 billion in criminal penalties for illegally marketing OxyContin, deceiving federal regulators, and paying kickbacks to doctors, with a judge ordering the company chairman to apologize directly to victims in court. Despite the corporate conviction, Sackler family members and company executives avoid any prison time or individual charges, drawing sharp criticism from families who lost loved ones to the opioid crisis. One article on coffee's effects on the gut-brain axis and mental health could not be fully accessed.

State-licensed medical cannabis operators face a hard June 22, 2026 deadline to file for DEA Schedule III registration or lose protected operating continuity, with the rescheduling also eliminating the Section 280E tax burden and potentially dropping effective tax rates from around 70-80% down to 20-30%. California cannabis vendors are publicly naming the state's lowest-rated operators on a so-called "shit list," though full details of the article were not accessible. Advocates argue that federal rescheduling now makes it illegal to deny medical cannabis patients housing, employment, healthcare or VA services, since agencies can no longer hide behind the old Schedule I "no accepted medical use" justification to discriminate.

Purdue Pharma got sentenced and ordered to pay $5.5 billion in criminal penalties for deceiving federal regulators and paying doctors kickbacks to boost OxyContin sales, fueling the opioid epidemic. A new Oxford-published study shows that minor cannabinoids CBC and CBG can boost silver's antimicrobial power by up to 64-fold against superbugs like MRSA, E. coli, and Pseudomonas, with clinical trials of the combination planned for late 2026. Swedish researchers found that salmon dosed with cocaine and its metabolite benzoylecgonine swam significantly faster and farther than sober fish, raising concerns about pharmaceutical pollution in waterways affecting wildlife behavior.

Canada's cannabis industry is flexing its global advantage, with surviving companies benefiting from world-class facilities built during the investor boom and years of experience in heavy regulation that new competitors can't easily replicate. The FDA could approve the first psychedelic therapy as early as late summer or fall 2026, with Compass Pathways' synthetic psilocybin for treatment-resistant depression leading the pack after receiving a National Priority Voucher that cuts review time to one or two months. Following the DOJ's April 22 order moving medical cannabis to Schedule III, Section 280E tax relief now applies to state-licensed medical operations for the full 2026 tax year, but adult-use businesses still face effective federal tax rates that can top 70%.
